summary: The southern parcel of the PG&E-owned Hoedown Yard along 22nd Street, drawn as one flexibly zoned parcel 'HDY1/2' in the D4D height figure (65 ft) and shown as commercial in the D4D Mid-Point scenario; like HDY3 it is outside Brookfield's 28-Acre Project and depends on the City exercising its option to buy the yard from PG&E. No sale, developer or construction has been recorded.

milestones.text: Mayor Lee and Supervisor Cohen introduce resolutions of intention to form Infrastructure and Revitalization Financing District No. 2 (Hoedown Yard) to finance affordable housing within Pier 70 and Parcel K South
Capital Planning Committee briefed on the resolutions of intent to form the Hoedown Yard IRFD and issue bonds
Port Commission consents to zoning the Hoedown Yard (Assessor's Blocks 4120/002 and 4711/008A per the memo) into the Pier 70 Special Use District (Resolution 17-45) and recommends the IRFD (17-49)

Board of Supervisors resolution of intention (File 170880) calls a public hearing for October 24, 2017 on formation of Infrastructure and Revitalization Financing District No. 2 (Hoedown Yard); the Port's Sept 2017 packet only schedules the hearing, and whether it was held that day was not confirmed

Port staff report (memo dated Aug 7, 2026) says the Hoedown Yard IRFD tax increment, one of three gap-funding sources for the affordable sites, is 'currently unavailable as market-rate development has yet to occur'

Port Commission Resolution 17-45 consents to zoning amendments establishing the Pier 70 Special Use District over the 28-Acre Site, the 20th & Illinois Street Parcel and the PG&E-owned Hoedown Yard, and approves the Design for Development, bringing the Hoedown Yard into the SUD land-use and height framework as a future development parcel; the Hoedown Yard is not part of FC Pier 70's 28-Acre Project DDA

facts.value: Pacific Gas and Electric Company (approximately 3.6-acre parcel per the D4D, 'approximately 3-acre' per the DDA terms, including a 0.2-acre unbuilt Michigan Street right-of-way easement); the City has an option to purchase

Flexible: shown as commercial in the D4D Mid-Point and Maximum Office scenarios and residential in the Maximum Residential scenario; Retail and Service frontage for HDY3 and HDY1/2 may be combined on 22nd Street
no more than six residential stories (D4D S6.4.2)

To be subdivided into three separate parcels and offered for sale by the City; the City may ask the Hoedown Yard developer to build Irish Hill Park, paid with special taxes and the Port's share of tax increment (2017 DDA major terms)
In the Pier 70 SUD but not part of the 28-Acre Project or the developer's option
Infrastructure and Revitalization Financing District No. 2 (Hoedown Yard), whose tax increment may fund affordable housing (unlike the Port IFD)

Named for the PG&E-owned 'Hoedown Yard' (HDY) parcel at Illinois and 22nd streets; the D4D describes the yard as currently owned by PG&E, with a City option to acquire it if PG&E can find a new location for its heavy industrial use

open_questions: Whether the City has exercised its option to buy the Hoedown Yard from PG&E, and whether the IRFD was actually formed after the October 24, 2017 hearing: no Port or Board document after 2017 mentioning either was found.
The Port's 2026 phasing exhibit leaves the Hoedown Yard and PKS uncolored (they are not developer parcels), so no phase is recorded here.
Assessor block/lot for the yard is given as 4120/002 and 4711/008A in the 2017 memo but 4120/002 and 4110/008A in the D4D; one is a typo, unresolved.

No basis for an expected-completion date was found: the Hoedown Yard is explicitly treated as a separate transaction outside the 28-Acre Project's DDA Schedule of Performance (Port Commission Item 11A, Aug 3, 2017, p.1) and the Port's 2026 proposed phasing exhibit leaves it uncolored; no Port or Board document after the 2017 resolutions of intent addresses a schedule for the City's still-unexercised PG&E purchase option, so this record stays undated rather than borrow the 28-Acre Project's buildout target.
